title: probabilistic-correlation-id-recovery-and-lossy-log-reassembly
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We observe 1-2% of production logs arrive without a stable correlation_id (missing or overwritten by sidecars), causing broken traces, inflated error rates in dashboards, and hard-to-debug user sessions. Existing strict-correlation pipelines drop or silo these events, losing signal.

Goal: Implement a probabilistic correlation-id recovery and lossy reassembly stage in the telemetry ingest pipeline that: (1) recovers likely correlation identifiers using deterministic heuristics + bloom-filtered trace fingerprints, (2) attaches a confidence score, (3) performs best-effort reassembly of fragmented multi-line events, and (4) tags events for downstream dashboards and Loki/ELK sinks without altering authoritative IDs.

Design summary:
- Ingest adapter (stateless): compute candidate correlation keys from available metadata (request_id, span_id, tenant_id, parent_service hints, timestamp windows).
- Recovery engine (stateful, short TTL): maintain sliding window of recent trace fingerprints (hashed sequences of span/service pairs) sharded by tenant and time bucket. Use an LRU + count-min sketch to prioritize low-memory candidates.
- Confidence scoring: combine source quality score (sidecar header present, sampled-trace flag) with fingerprint match score. Confidence encoded as 0-100.
- Reassembly: lossy reassembly attempts to merge contiguous log fragments within a 2s window using sequence hints (chunk_index, partial_marker) and content similarity (Jaccard token overlap). If ambiguous, emit both fragments with linked_reassembly_id and confidence flags instead of mutating content.
- Downstream: Enriched events include recovered_correlation_id, recovered_confidence, reassembly_id, and reassembly_confidence. Router rules in the pipeline will forward to Loki label sets and an ELK index mapping, but authoritative correlation_id (when present) is never overwritten.

Trade-offs considered:
- Memory vs recall: using count-min sketch reduces memory but increases false positives; mitigated via conservative confidence threshold for dashboard aggregation.
- Privacy: fingerprinting uses hashed service/span tuples and truncates to 128-bit to avoid PII.
- Complexity vs observability: added stage increases latency by ~5-12ms p95; acceptable within current SLO for non-API-critical paths but gated behind rollout flags.

Acceptance criteria:
- Recovered correlation IDs increase trace-join rate by >= 40% on sampled test logs without raising false-link rate >3% (measured on synthetic injection).
- End-to-end p95 ingest latency increase < 15ms for 99% of requests under nominal load.
- Dashboard error-rate spike attributable to stray correlation drops reduced by >= 30% in A/B rollout.
- Feature toggle and telemetry (recovery_count, false_positive_estimate, average_confidence) exposed in Console.
- Unit/integration tests + canary run completed and documented in Confluence.
